The chajchas (also written chapchas; Spanish uñas, meaning hooves) are a small rattle-like percussion instrument, Hornbostel–Sachs 112.1. Dried goat or sheep hooves are strung on coloured cloth, often elastic, that can be worn on the wrist or ankle; they are usually used in pairs and sounded by shaking. The instrument comes from the central Andes and is used in traditional rites and ceremonies; it is also common in the folk music of Colombia, Bolivia, Peru, Chile and Ecuador, and can be used in ritual dance.
